title: Redmi Buds 6 Play: Cheap, Long-Lasting Earbuds for Everyday Listening
summary: The Redmi Buds 6 Play is Xiaomi's cheapest true wireless model: 3.6 g per earbud, up to 36 hours with the case, Bluetooth 5.4 and IPX4 — but no active noise cancellation, no transparency mode, no custom EQ, and a 180 ms low-latency mode that Xiaomi only lists for a handful of its own phones. Here's who it suits, what's missing and how it compares with the Redmi Buds 6 Active, Buds 6 Lite and SoundPEATS T3 Pro.
description:
## Who is it for?

- Students and first-time wireless earbud buyers on a minimal budget.
- Anyone who wants a light, cheap backup pair for calls, classes and podcasts.
- Listeners who value battery life over noise cancellation.

## Why consider it?

- Up to 7.5 hours per charge and 36 hours with the case (Xiaomi, 50% volume).
- Only 3.6 g per earbud, with silicone tips in three sizes.
- Bluetooth 5.4, Google Fast Pair and five EQ presets in the Xiaomi Earbuds app.

sections.title: What is the Redmi Buds 6 Play?
sections.content:
The Redmi Buds 6 Play (model M2420E1) is the entry model in Xiaomi's Redmi Buds 6 family, sold in markets including the UK, EU, Australia, the Middle East, Africa and much of Asia. It comes in black, white, blue and pink, and competes on price with unbranded earbuds sold on marketplaces — the difference being an established brand, a companion app and a proper spec sheet.

It's worth knowing what that low price buys and what it doesn't. Xiaomi has put its effort into battery life and comfort: a 600 mAh case, 7.5 hours per charge and 3.6 g earbuds. Everything that costs money in an earbud — active noise cancellation, a transparency mode, AAC or LDAC, multipoint, wireless charging — is absent or unlisted. If you read the spec sheet with that in mind, it's easy to tell whether this is enough for you.

sections.title: Design, fit and comfort
sections.content:
Xiaomi lists each earbud at 3.6 g and the whole set at 40 g, and the case is a compact 53.9 × 53.9 × 27.4 mm rounded square that slips into a jeans pocket. The bean shape sits in the bowl of the ear without a stem, with silicone tips (S and L in the box, M fitted) sealing the ear canal. HiFi Report's roundup of owner impressions describes them as comfortable for hours, and contrasts this with the Redmi Buds 6 Active, which has no silicone tips and was harder to wear for long periods.

Two caveats. First, stemless beans rely entirely on a good seal; try all three tip sizes, because the right one improves both bass and stability. Second, read the IPX4 small print: Xiaomi says the rating covers the earbuds only, not the case, and actually advises avoiding strenuous exercise because heavy sweat may cause damage. These are fine for a walk or a light gym session, not for long runs in the heat or for showering.

sections.title: Sound, codec and app
sections.content:
Each earbud uses a 10 mm dynamic driver tuned, according to Xiaomi, by its own acoustic lab. HiFi Report's summary of user reviews describes smooth, present bass with balanced mids and highs for the price — a consumer tuning that suits pop, podcasts and video rather than critical listening.

Xiaomi doesn't list any codec. Its battery footnote says testing was done with SBC, and AAC is never mentioned, so the realistic assumption is SBC only. On Android that's normal at this price; on an iPhone, which prefers AAC, it means slightly lower quality and occasionally higher latency than an AAC pair such as the SoundPEATS T3 Pro.

The Xiaomi Earbuds app (Android and iOS) offers five presets — standard, enhance bass, enhance voice, enhance treble and enhance volume — plus touch-control settings. There is no custom or graphic EQ, which reviewers list as a drawback. 'Enhance voice' is the useful one for lectures and podcasts; 'enhance volume' helps on noisy streets but will make music sound harsher.

sections.title: Battery, calls, latency — and no ANC
sections.content:
Battery is the standout. Xiaomi rates 7.5 hours per charge and 36 hours with the case, measured at 50% volume with SBC, and 10 minutes in the case gives about 3 hours — but only when the case itself has at least 35% charge. Because there's no ANC drawing power, those numbers are realistic for real-world listening at moderate volume; louder playback and long calls will shorten them. One owner quoted by HiFi Report went about two weeks between case charges with roughly an hour of use a day.

For calls, AI noise reduction filters background noise so the other person hears your voice more clearly. It does nothing to reduce what you hear — there is no active noise cancellation and no transparency mode. On a bus or train you simply turn the volume up, which is not great for your hearing over time. Owner feedback on the microphones is mixed.

Latency needs a closer look. Xiaomi advertises a 180 ms low-latency mode, but its footnote lists support only on the Xiaomi 14 Ultra, 14, 13, 13 Pro, 13 Ultra and POCO F6. On other phones, including iPhones and most Samsung models, expect standard Bluetooth latency — fine for video (apps compensate) but noticeable in rhythm games and shooters. Xiaomi doesn't list multipoint either, so treat it as one device at a time.

sections.title: Redmi Buds 6 Play vs Buds 6 Active, Buds 6 Lite and SoundPEATS T3 Pro
sections.content:
**Redmi Buds 6 Active:** a semi-in-ear design without silicone tips, a larger 14.2 mm driver, 6 hours per charge and 30 hours with the case, and — like the Play — no ANC (Xiaomi lists only call noise reduction). Choose the Active if you dislike tips sealing your ears; choose the Play for a better seal, longer battery and, per HiFi Report's owner roundup, better comfort and bass.

**Redmi Buds 6 Lite:** the cheapest Redmi Buds 6 model with real ANC — Xiaomi rates it at up to 40 dB — plus a 12.4 mm driver, 7 hours per charge and 38 hours with the case (measured with AAC), at 4.2 g per earbud. If you commute, this is the Xiaomi step up to look at. Note that the Lite uses Bluetooth 5.3.

**SoundPEATS T3 Pro** (reviewed separately on this site): adds ANC, a transparency mode, AAC, a 12 mm driver, four microphones and a game mode; reviewers and buyers also report multipoint, though SoundPEATS' spec list doesn't state it. The trade-off is battery: SoundPEATS rates about 7 hours per charge and 28 hours total with ANC off, and Allround Review reports roughly 5 hours with ANC on. The T3 Pro is also slightly heavier at 4.15 g per earbud. Choose the Redmi for maximum battery and the lowest price; choose the T3 Pro if noise, iPhone use or transparency matters.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't
sections.content:
Buy it if you want your first wireless earbuds on a minimal budget; need a light pair for lectures, podcasts, calls and video; want a cheap backup to keep in a bag; or care more about going days between charges than about blocking noise.

Skip it if you commute on noisy transport (the Buds 6 Lite or SoundPEATS T3 Pro offer ANC); play competitive mobile games on a phone that isn't on Xiaomi's low-latency list; use an iPhone and want AAC; need to switch between a phone and a laptop without re-pairing; or want a custom EQ and better microphones.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used these earbuds in person. This is a research roundup, updated November 2026, based on Xiaomi's global overview and specification pages for the Redmi Buds 6 Play, Buds 6 Active and Buds 6 Lite (including their footnotes on battery tests, low-latency support and IPX4), and HiFi Report's collection of owner and reviewer impressions. Figures for the SoundPEATS T3 Pro come from SoundPEATS' official page and Allround Review. Battery and latency figures are Xiaomi's, not our measurements. Images are official Xiaomi product photos.

sections.title: Should you buy the Redmi Buds 6 Play?
sections.content: For everyday listening on the smallest budget, yes. Long, realistic battery life, very light earbuds, Bluetooth 5.4, Fast Pair and a basic EQ app from a major brand are a sensible package. Just be clear about what you're not getting: no ANC, no transparency, no AAC, no custom EQ, no listed multipoint, and a low-latency mode that only works on a few Xiaomi phones. If any of those matter, spend a little more on the Redmi Buds 6 Lite or the SoundPEATS T3 Pro.

pros: Long battery life: 7.5 h per charge and 36 h with the case (Xiaomi, 50% volume).
Fast charging: 10 minutes for about 3 hours when the case has at least 35% charge.
Very light 3.6 g earbuds with silicone tips in three sizes; owners describe them as comfortable for hours.
Bluetooth 5.4 and Google Fast Pair for quick pairing on Android.
Xiaomi Earbuds app with five EQ presets and touch customisation on Android and iOS.
Very low price for a major brand, with a full official spec sheet.
cons: No active noise cancellation or transparency mode — call noise reduction only.
The 180 ms low-latency mode is listed only for six Xiaomi/POCO phones.
No AAC or LDAC listed (Xiaomi's battery tests use SBC); no multipoint listed.
Five presets only — no custom EQ; owner feedback on the microphones is mixed.
IPX4 covers the earbuds only, and Xiaomi advises avoiding strenuous exercise.
No wireless charging, and Xiaomi's box contents don't list a USB-C cable.

faq.question: Does the Redmi Buds 6 Play have ANC?
faq.answer: No. Its AI noise reduction only cleans up your voice on calls. For ANC in the same family, look at the Redmi Buds 6 Lite (rated up to 40 dB by Xiaomi).

faq.question: How long does the battery last?
faq.answer: Xiaomi rates up to 7.5 hours per charge and 36 hours with the case at 50% volume with SBC. A 10-minute charge gives about 3 hours if the case has at least 35% battery.

faq.question: Does it work with iPhone?
faq.answer: Yes, over standard Bluetooth, and the Xiaomi Earbuds app is on iOS. Google Fast Pair is Android-only, AAC isn't listed and the low-latency mode is limited to certain Xiaomi phones.

faq.question: Is it good for gaming?
faq.answer: Fine for casual games and video. The 180 ms low-latency mode only works on the Xiaomi phones Xiaomi lists; elsewhere, latency will be noticeable in shooters and rhythm games.

faq.question: Redmi Buds 6 Play or Redmi Buds 6 Active?
faq.answer: The Play seals the ear with silicone tips and has a bigger battery (36 h vs 30 h). The Active is semi-in-ear with a 14.2 mm driver for people who dislike tips. Neither has ANC.

faq.question: Redmi Buds 6 Play or SoundPEATS T3 Pro?
faq.answer: Choose the Redmi for longer battery and the lowest price. Choose the SoundPEATS T3 Pro if you want ANC, transparency, AAC for iPhone and reviewer-reported multipoint, accepting shorter battery life with ANC on.
